engagement_title: Velvet Hour monthly gig package: cut last month's single camera set take into a social piece and a vertical, bring four self supplied act photographs and one dark house still to one room look, recover the moth and lamp mark off a painted lamp box, and merge this month's four listing cards out of the printer's own file
vertical: Arts, culture and live music. A monthly ticketed jazz and folk night in the ninety seat back room of a bar, Providence, Rhode Island
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post for a recurring live music editor and promo designer quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, a small venue that films one session a month for its social channels and needs both a short social edit and printed promo for the next lineup, with a stated house style of 'clean, coherent, story-first, no gimmicks' and distribution across Instagram, Facebook and YouTube. The real post named no venue, so the line is laundered to the fictional Velvet Hour monthly night (a moth and lamp mark) with four fictional acts: Junie Ash, The Paper Kestrels, Odette Vann and Cinder and Salt. The ledger's repositioning note stops mid sentence at 'REPOSITIONED for co', and the reposition it was reaching for is the honest one: the real post asked for a recurring package, so the commission is written as the FIRST month of that recurring package, and the parts of it the connector cannot do (assembling a multi angle edit, adding motion graphics, extracting a frame from the take) are replaced by the parts it verifiably can (index, shorten, clean speech, reframe without enlarging; grade a mixed set to one look; recover a lost mark off a photograph; reverse engineer the printer's card into a live merge template). CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the fuller commission honest, because HTML authoring now yields a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes and prepare_indd_merge_template builds a real merge template from a bare press PDF.
client_one_liner: We film one set a month and then spend a week scrambling to turn it into something we can post and something we can print, and this month our logo file is gone, the four acts sent us photographs that look like four different venues, and the cards go to the printer on Friday.
client_brief:
Velvet Hour, the monthly package

Velvet Hour is one night a month in the back room of a bar in Providence. Ninety seats, two sets, no support. We film the second set on one camera from the same corner every month and somebody takes pictures from the bar. Then we scramble. We would like to stop scrambling, so treat this month as the first one you would do, and set it up so we can ask for the same thing again.

From last month's take we need a short piece for our channels that makes someone who was not there want the next ticket, and a tall version of it for stories. The take is long and a lot of it is people tuning. We are not precious about which moments you use. We are precious about whether what you use holds up standing on its own.

Our host says a few words at the top. It is worth keeping if it can be made listenable. The room is loud, the mic is a cheap one on a stand, and there is a fridge behind the bar.

Next month's four acts sent us their own photographs. They look like four different venues, which is exactly what they are. They need to look like our room instead: warm, low, close, unhurried. Somebody also got a picture of last month's singer under the lamp that we think could carry a poster, though it was very dark in there.

The lamp and moth mark only exists as paint on the lamp box by the door now. The file went with the designer who made it. We need it back as artwork rather than as a photograph of paint, because it goes on the card and it goes on the poster.

The listing card is the same card our printer has made for three seasons, one act to a card. We have his file and we have the four acts as a list. We need this month's four.

Tickets are eighteen to twenty five dollars and the crowd is thirty to sixty, people who read a lineup carefully. It should look like a good room, not a club. Tell us what you did so we can ask for it again.
price_band_and_audience: An eighteen to twenty five dollar ticket in a ninety seat back room, audience thirty to sixty and lineup literate. The band is load bearing. At this price the night sells intimacy and musicianship, so the treatment has to be warm, low key, close and unhurried: lamp light left as lamp light, grain left in rather than fought, type quiet and editorial, the act's face doing the work. The same four acts at a fifteen dollar door in a two hundred capacity club would correctly be graded cold and contrasty with hard colour and a loud type scale, and shipping that here misrepresents a room where people sit down and listen, which loses the crowd the venue actually has. Push the other way into black tie restraint and gold foil gestures and it prices itself at a ninety dollar concert hall and reads as pretentious to a bar audience. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,600 dollars a month on retainer.

brand_identity.tagline: One night a month, sit down and listen.
brand_identity.sector: Arts, culture and live music (monthly ticketed jazz and folk night)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021 in the back room of a bar, Providence, Rhode Island. Tiny: two organisers, ninety seats, one night a month.
brand_identity.about: Velvet Hour is a monthly ticketed jazz and folk night held in the ninety seat back room of a Providence bar. Two sets, no support, one camera in the same corner every month. The night sells intimacy and musicianship to people who read a lineup carefully, so everything we make should feel like a good room rather than a club or a concert hall.
brand_identity.audience: Lineup literate adults roughly thirty to sixty who pay eighteen to twenty five dollars to sit close and listen. Locals who follow the acts, not a party crowd.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid, intimate. An eighteen to twenty five dollar ticket. Never budget club, never black tie concert hall.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet editorial system: a warm serif for act names and titles, a restrained humanist sans for billing lines, dates and body. Type stays small, generously set and calm. No display gimmicks, no gold foil gestures.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, affectionate, low key. Talks about the room and the players, never hypes. Short sentences, no exclamation, lets the act's face and the music do the work.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our mark, a moth over a lamp inside a hairline arc of small caps type, was made by the designer who set up the night, and the source file went with them when they left. All that survives is the mark painted in one cream ink on the dark green lamp box by the door, which is why it has to be rebuilt from that as real artwork. No brand typeface was ever formally chosen, so the type system is open for you to set.
brand_identity.values: Story first, no gimmicks. Clean, coherent, honest to the room. We would rather look like a place people sit and listen than like a night that is trying too hard.

assets_supplied.name: velvet_hour_set_take.mp4 (47 minutes, single camera, 1920 x 1080, house desk audio mixed with one room mic)
assets_supplied.kind: The full second set filmed from the same corner of the room the venue always films from, one locked off camera, no cuts.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The second set, one camera, same corner as always. Most of it is people tuning."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The camera sits off axis to clear a pillar, so the performers hold the left third of the frame and their position drifts across the set (at the mic downstage left for two numbers, on the stool nearer centre for the rest), which means a tall reframe can be technically clean and contain nothing but an amp stack and an empty stool. The host's introduction also runs straight into the first number with no gap, and the room mic carries a steady fridge hum under it.

assets_supplied.name: velvet_hour_house_stills/ (11 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photographs taken from the bar during the same set at very high sensitivity under a single tungsten lamp.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Pictures from the bar on the night. The one of the singer under the lamp might carry a poster."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The lamp throws a heavy warm cast across the singer's face, so a whole frame move toward a neutral room look takes her skin grey while leaving the lamp itself orange, and the frames are noisy in a way no tool here reduces. Two of the eleven are the same moment a third of a second apart, and the sharper of the two is the one where her eyes are closed.

assets_supplied.name: next_month_act_photos/ (4 frames, one per act, supplied by the acts)
assets_supplied.kind: Publicity photographs sent in by Junie Ash, The Paper Kestrels, Odette Vann and Cinder and Salt, each shot by whoever they had.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the four acts sent us. Use them as they are, we cannot go back and ask."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They are not comparable inputs: two are full scale camera files, one is a screengrab off a phone at roughly nine hundred pixels on the long edge, and one is a photograph of a printed press sheet that carries the printer's screen and grows a moire once it is graded. Nothing in the filenames, the list or the client's description separates them, and the small one binds into the card's photograph frame without any complaint from anything.

assets_supplied.name: velvet_hour_lampbox.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Daylight photograph, taken at an angle, of the venue's mark painted in one cream ink on the dark green lamp box beside the door: a moth over a lamp inside a hairline arc of small caps type.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark. It is paint on the lamp box now, that is all that is left of it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound mark on a photographed painted substrate, so a prompt naming the box returns the box, a prompt naming the whole mark returns the moth and the lamp while silently dropping the arc of type, and the wing counters are enclosed so a background knockout hands back a filled slab rather than a see through mark. The paint is also laid on thickest at the wing edges, which is not visible in the photograph and does not show in a trace viewed at canvas size.

assets_supplied.name: velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the venue's printer has used for the listing card for three seasons, one act to a card, with a photograph well and four blocks of type.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The printer's own file. Same card three seasons running, one act per card."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Printed it reads as four separate blocks (the act name, a one line billing, the date and door time, and a short paragraph) plus a photograph, but the artwork is one continuous flow, so what the conversion actually exposes as editable frames looks nothing like the printed page. The structure readout also omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed, every offset past it is short, and the validator still calls the mapping valid.

assets_supplied.name: velvet_hour_lineup.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Plain data: the four acts, their billing lines, the date, the door time and the ticket price.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The four acts as our booker keeps them. The billing lines are theirs, do not rewrite them."

acceptance_bar: The short social piece stands on its own to somebody who was not in the room: it opens on something happening, not on tuning, and it does not end mid phrase.
The tall version contains the performer for its whole length. A vertical that is technically correct and framed on an empty stool and an amp stack is a failed deliverable, not a near miss.

No delivered video is taller or wider than the source it came from, and no delivered image exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions. Anything that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
The host's introduction is listenable end to end and still sounds like a room with people in it rather than a voice recorded in a booth.

The four act photographs read as four acts playing the same room: one warmth, one black point, one distance from the face. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
The poster still keeps the lamp as lamp light and keeps the singer's skin as skin. Neutralising the room is a wrong answer here.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and its wing counters still open at the size it actually lands on the poster and on the card.
All four listing cards carry every field the printer's card carries, on all four, with the correct act's photograph on the correct act's card.
The four cards come back as one press file in the booker's row order, one act per page, page count equal to row count.
The poster and the two social canvases sit in ONE editable working file, each keeping its own canvas size, and the self contained source it was built from is delivered alongside it.
One type system across the poster, the social set and the card, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.

The note is a recipe the venue can hand back next month: what was applied to which photograph and why it differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, what was done to the take and the audio, and anything about the recovered mark they need to know.

adobe_surfaces.role: The headline deliverable. A forty seven minute single camera take is indexed rather than watched, then shortened rather than assembled, because the cutter only removes: it never lengthens, never reorders and it chooses its own spans. The host's introduction is lifted out of a loud room with a fridge in it, and the tall version is reached by reframing a sixteen by nine source without ever enlarging it, which is the constraint that decides how much of the performer can be kept.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision. It fixes one room look off the best act photograph and brings the other three toward it one call at a time rather than batching one parameter set across four different cameras, confines the correction on the poster still so the lamp stays lamp light while the face comes back, prepares the card photographs at the size the merge actually needs, and recovers the mark at ink level off a photographed painted box with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign, template archaeology and data merge
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and again as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The four listing cards, built by reverse engineering the printer's own press PDF into a live merge template, because no native InDesign file exists anywhere in the venue. The IDML round trip is the only honest channel for what the converted document really contains, the mapping has to be computed against the true story text rather than the readout, the photograph column has to bind per row, and the delivery route has to be the one that preserves the booker's row order.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The poster and the two social canvases as one native editable document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the recovered mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, family and weight are declared per element, and the payload travels by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system spanning the poster, the social set and the printed card. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on a warm listening room rather than a club night. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name has to be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The cards are a genuine one record per page run and belong in the merge; the poster and the social canvases are designed one offs and belong in authored HTML because the venue has to edit them next month. The brief pins both destinations, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the take, the eleven house stills, the four act photographs, the lamp box frame, the printer PDF and the lineup data, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, but the manifest has to survive forty artefacts, so it is keyed by role rather than by filename.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Index the forty seven minute take: get a content readout of where the numbers are, where the tuning is, and where the host's introduction sits.
trajectory.judgement: Nobody is going to watch forty seven minutes, and the take carries no markers. The index is the only map of the material, and it is also the only place the shape of the set (how long the songs run, how much dead air sits between them) becomes visible.
trajectory.produces: A content index of the take with the host's introduction located.

trajectory.action: Cut the social piece down from the take to the social length, accepting that the tool only shortens and picks its own spans.
trajectory.judgement: There is no assembly here and no timeline. The lever is the target length, and the target length is a taste decision about what an eighteen dollar listening room sells: long enough for a phrase to land, short enough that nobody scrolls.
trajectory.produces: A short social cut derived from the take with its chosen length recorded.

trajectory.action: Clean the host's introduction so it is listenable without turning it into a booth recording.
trajectory.judgement: The venue asked for listenable, not broadcast. The fridge and the room are two different things and only one of them is the problem; a treatment that takes the room out with the hum has removed the thing the venue is selling.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned introduction track judged against the untreated original.

trajectory.action: Produce the tall version by reframing the cut for stories, without enlarging anything.
trajectory.judgement: A sixteen by nine source reframed tall keeps its height and loses its width, so the only question that matters is which strip of width survives. The camera is off axis, so the geometric centre is not where the performer is.
trajectory.produces: A vertical cut at or below the source height, with the reframe decision recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview the four act photographs and the eleven house stills and triage them: which are camera files, which is a screengrab, which is a photograph of print, which house frame can actually carry a poster, and which two are the same moment.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts four usable photographs and a poster still. The pictures are the only place that can be settled, and reading them is not the same as counting files. The act photograph that carries a printer's screen will fight everything done to it later.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering source scale, illuminant, screen artefacts and duplicate moments.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and a handheld bar photograph is rarely level.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one room look off the best act photograph and bring the other three toward it with their own calls, recording the parameters applied to each.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not four good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for four frames shot by four people in four rooms; the agent has to hold one destination and reach it by four different routes, and decide how far a frame is worth pushing before it is named instead.
trajectory.produces: Four act masters on one room look with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine the correction on the poster still so the lamp keeps its own colour while the singer's face comes back, selecting by the material's visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the lamp as an object pulls the selection to the fixture. A whole frame neutralisation here would deliver a technically clean picture of a room that never looked like that.
trajectory.produces: A poster still where the lamp reads as lamp light and the face reads as skin.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the lamp box: an ink level selection naming the paint's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own bounding box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the paint and not the box, which polarity to trace, and whether the compound mark comes back in one selection or has to be taken element by element. A background knockout is the wrong instrument on an enclosed wing counter.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a note of which elements it actually contains.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against an eighteen to twenty five dollar listening room and a lineup literate crowd. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's press PDF, round trip it to IDML, and read the real frame inventory before promising any mapping: how many text frames exist, what each one actually holds, and whether a graphic frame is there at all.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about what the converted document exposes. Promising a per field mapping before looking is how a template gets built against a page that does not exist.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory with counts, bounds, applied faces and existing links.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the true story text from the document's own stories, compute every offset from that string, build the mapping, run it back through the validator, prepare the template, then round trip the result again and confirm every expected placeholder is genuinely present.
trajectory.judgement: The readout of a story is not the story. Both the validator and the prepare step report success on a mapping that has already lost fields, so the only evidence that a template is complete is finding the placeholders in the document itself.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed present by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Merge the four records with the prepared act photographs bound per row, deliver as one press file in the booker's row order one act per page, and render proofs for sign off.
trajectory.judgement: Order and identity are the deliverable here. The route that preserves row order is not the route that produces the fastest proofs, and the photograph column binds only in one exact shape.
trajectory.produces: One four page press file plus per record proofs, with the correct photograph on the correct card.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes, inline every photograph as image data, place the mark as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much dark the poster carries and how large the mark actually sits.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the poster and both social canvases, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for canvases two and three.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the other two.

trajectory.action: Write the monthly recipe note: what was applied to which photograph and why, what was done to the take and to the audio, every resize any tool reported, the type system by role, and what the recovered mark does and does not contain.
trajectory.judgement: The venue explicitly wants to ask for this again. A note that only lists outputs is worth nothing next month; the note has to be specific enough that the same package can be reproduced against a different set of acts.
trajectory.produces: A written recipe note the booker can hand back next month.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the tall version actually contains a performer. The cutter chooses its own spans, so which moments of a forty seven minute set end up in the social piece is not the agent's decision and is not knowable until the cut comes back. The camera sits off axis to clear a pillar and the performers drift across the set, at the mic downstage left for two numbers and on the stool nearer centre for the rest, so where the subject sits in the frame is different in different moments of the same take. The reframe reports success and returns a clean, correctly sized vertical either way. Whether that vertical holds the singer or holds an amp stack and an empty stool is a property of which spans the cut happened to select, and it is visible only by looking at the reframed result.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering dodges it and no parameter prevents it, because the span selection belongs to the tool and the reframe has no subject argument; running the reframe first on the full take would answer a different question, since the full take contains both positions. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the venue is not precious about which moments are used and asks only that whatever is used holds up, which is an art direction requirement, not a disclosure that the camera is off axis. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different route: re cut to a different target length so a different set of spans survives, or abandon the automatic cut for the vertical and build it from a span where the performer is where the vertical needs her, accepting a shorter piece.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re cut the social piece at a different length and re reframe, or split the two deliverables so the vertical comes from a different span than the wide one, then re judge whether the wide cut and the vertical still read as the same night.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A stories vertical delivered at the correct dimensions, reported successful at every step, that shows a monthly music night as an empty stool and a corner of an amplifier.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually becomes when it is converted. On the page it reads as four separate blocks of type plus a photograph well, and everything about a per field merge assumes those blocks are separate frames. Frame granularity out of a PDF is not under the agent's control: a continuous text flow can collapse into a single text frame holding every line, and a photograph well can arrive with or without a usable graphic frame. Neither is inspectable in the PDF, neither is reported by the conversion, and the conversion succeeds identically either way. Only the round tripped document says what is really there.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not avoid it and no option controls it; converting earlier only learns the same thing earlier, and there is no parameter that asks for four frames. Doing it right the first time is not available because the right thing to do depends on the answer. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the printer has made the same card for three seasons, one act per card, which is a description of the printed object, not of its internal structure. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a structurally different mapping strategy: offset based replacement computed inside one story instead of a field per frame mapping, with every offset recomputed against the reconstructed story text, plus a separate decision about whether the photograph can bind at all or has to reach the card another way.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Discard the planned per frame mapping, reconstruct the true story text, recompute every offset against it in descending order, rebuild and revalidate the mapping, re prepare the template, round trip again to confirm the placeholders landed, and re decide the photograph route before any record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Four cards that convert, validate, prepare and merge with success reported at every stage, and arrive at the printer on Friday missing the door time and the billing line on all four, which nobody sees until the cards are cut.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the size it actually reproduces. The trace is clean at canvas size: the moth reads, the lamp reads, the counters in the wings are open. The paint on the lamp box is laid on thickest at the wing edges, which is invisible in the photograph and invisible in the trace viewed whole, and at the size the mark actually lands on the poster and at social scale those counters close and the moth becomes a dark lozenge on the poster's dark ground. The vector is correct, the export reports success, and the rendition shows only the first canvas, so the mark on the two social canvases can be judged only from the returned markup and by looking at it at its real size rather than at the size it was drawn.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that avoids it and no option that prevents it, because the tracing tool takes no parameters at all: the only lever is the raster preparation, and how much the paint will bloom is a property of this photograph of this painted box. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the mark back as artwork rather than as a photograph of paint and says it goes on the card and the poster; it never suggests the mark might not hold. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different upstream asset: re prepare the raster with a tighter ink level selection and re trace, or deliver a reduced mark for small use (the moth and lamp without the hairline arc of type) and re compose the canvases around whichever version survives.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare and re trace the mark, or cut a second small use variant, strip the opaque path and re inject the viewBox on whatever comes back, re author the HTML around the surviving version, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A poster and a social set delivered as an editable file in which the venue's mark is a dark blob on a dark ground at every size anybody will actually see it, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: Velvet Hour social cut and stories vertical
deliverables.spec: One short social piece derived from last month's forty seven minute single camera take, opening on something happening rather than on tuning and not ending mid phrase, plus a vertical version for stories that holds the performer for its whole length. Both at or below the source dimensions, with the chosen lengths and the reframe decision recorded. This is one motion set, not one clip at two sizes: the vertical is judged on whether it stands alone.

deliverables.name: Velvet Hour house photography, four acts and the poster still
deliverables.spec: Four act photographs from four different sources brought to one room look (one warmth, one black point, one distance from the face) plus the poster still from the night with the lamp kept as lamp light and the singer's skin kept as skin, and the card sized preparations of each act photograph. Per frame parameter log including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours, and a named exclusion for any frame that could not be brought to the set.

deliverables.name: Recovered moth and lamp mark
deliverables.spec: The compound mark recovered from a photograph of paint on a lamp box as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, wing counters open at the size the mark actually lands on the poster and at social scale, and an explicit statement of which elements of the lockup the recovered artwork does and does not contain.

deliverables.name: This month's four listing cards
deliverables.spec: One press file of four pages, one act per page, in the booker's row order, carrying every field the printer's card carries on all four records, with the correct act's prepared photograph bound to the correct act's card. Produced from a live merge template reverse engineered from the printer's own press PDF, delivered alongside per record proofs for sign off. Page count equal to row count is the checkable gate.

deliverables.name: Poster and social set as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes (the poster and two social canvases), with live editable text in one licensed type system, the recovered mark as real vector shapes, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self contained source HTML, which is the durable half, because the venue changes the acts and the date every month and cannot re commission.

deliverables.name: Monthly recipe note
deliverables.spec: A written note built to be handed back next month: what was applied to which photograph and why that frame differs from its neighbours, what was done to the take and to the audio and what was deliberately left in, every resize any tool reported with the file it applied to, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, and what the recovered mark contains, what it omits and where it should not be used.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered video exceeds the source take's frame height or width, and no delivered image exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the dimensions of every delivered file and compare each against the source it derives from, per the manifest.

verifiers_auto.text: No crop or resize tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry, and every downscaled entry is transcribed in the recipe note.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the tradeoffs objects captured from every image and video call against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The merged card file has exactly four pages and the pages are in the booker's row order.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the page count of the press file and check the act name on each page against the row order of the supplied lineup data.

verifiers_auto.text: Every field the printer's card carries is present on all four merged records, with no field silently absent.
verifiers_auto.how: Round trip the prepared template to IDML and grep the stories for every expected placeholder, then read all four merged pages for every field.

verifiers_auto.text: Each card carries its own act's photograph rather than one photograph repeated across the run.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare the bound image on each page against the per row photograph the agent prepared, by file identity rather than by position in any returned URL list.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered mark's SVG has a viewBox attribute and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned three slides, each keeping its own declared canvas size, with no image resolved to the importer's placeholder and the mark arriving as vector path shapes.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and per slide width and height in the export response, then parse the returned per slide markup for one by one placeholder image data and count path shape elements in the mark's region on each canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed PostScript face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_human.text: The short social piece makes somebody who was not there want the next ticket, and it neither opens on tuning nor ends mid phrase.
verifiers_human.how: Watch it once, cold, without the brief in front of you.

verifiers_human.text: The stories vertical holds the performer for its whole length rather than a corner of the stage.
verifiers_human.how: Play the vertical at phone size and watch where the subject sits across the whole duration.

verifiers_human.text: The host's introduction is listenable and still sounds like a room with people in it.
verifiers_human.how: Listen to the cleaned introduction against the untreated original on headphones.

verifiers_human.text: Laid side by side the four act photographs read as four acts playing the same room, not as four venues.
verifiers_human.how: Place the four at listing scale and judge warmth, black point and distance from the face as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The poster still keeps the lamp as lamp light and the singer as a person in a dark room.
verifiers_human.how: View the poster still at full size against the untreated frame.

verifiers_human.text: The mark still reads as the moth and lamp where it actually lands, on the poster ground and at social size.
verifiers_human.how: View the mark at its reproduction size on each canvas and on the card, never at full canvas.

verifiers_human.text: The whole package reads as an eighteen to twenty five dollar listening room, not as a club night and not as a concert hall.
verifiers_human.how: Judge grade, type scale, ground colour and pacing against the stated band and crowd.

verifiers_human.text: The recipe note would let a different freelancer produce next month's package without asking the venue anything.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that every decision and every limitation is named.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are motion work, which are raster work, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
How long the social piece should be, which is the only real lever over an automatic cut and is a taste decision about an intimate listening room rather than a technical one.
How much of the room to leave in the host's introduction, given that the hum and the room are not the same thing and only one of them is the problem.
Which strip of width the vertical keeps, on a take whose camera is off axis so the geometric centre is not where the performer is.
Whether the four act photographs are one set. The client believes they nearly are; laid in a row is the only place that can be settled.
How far to push the screengrab and the photograph of print before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them in the note.
Whether to neutralise the poster still or to confine the correction and keep the lamp, which is the difference between a technically clean picture and a picture of that room.

Selection wording on the lamp box: naming the box takes the box, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and a background knockout on an enclosed wing counter is the wrong instrument entirely.
Whether the compound mark comes back in one selection or has to be taken element by element, and which version carries which application.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a listening room band and a lineup literate crowd, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Which merge delivery route is used, given that one route preserves the booker's row order and another returns records whose labels do not match their contents.
How much dark the poster carries. At this band restraint is the design, and a loud, high contrast, benefit led poster is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of a band in a bar. IDENTITY: these are next month's four actual acts with their own publicity photographs and their own billing lines, and last month's actual singer under the venue's actual lamp; a regenerated performer is somebody else on the poster and a regenerated mark is another venue's logo, when the mark has to be RECOVERED off paint rather than reinvented. SPEC: the printer needs four pages in the booker's row order with every field present and the correct act's photograph on the correct act's card, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for, and the stories deliverable is a reframe of real footage that must never be enlarged. EDITABILITY: the poster and social set are defined by being editable, since the venue changes the acts and the date every single month and explicitly cannot re commission. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: does this vertical actually contain the performer, does this converted card expose the frames the printed page implies, do the moth's wing counters still open at the size anybody will see them.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. PREMIERE: the four sanctioned video and audio tools are used strictly inside their verified envelope, media_summarize as the content index, video_create_quick_cut which only SHORTENS (it never lengthens, never reorders and never trims to a timestamp), media_enhance_speech on the spoken introduction only, and video_resize which never enlarges. No frame is extracted from the take (the poster still is a photograph taken on the night), no format is converted, no timeline is assembled, and no deliverable depends on any capability outside those four. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, remove_background and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls; the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry (154,926 px card mask versus 9,372 px ink mask on the same frame), the compound mark partial selection that silently drops an element, the solid disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed counter, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings, and the acceptance bar scores exactly the hygiene the tool does not perform. INDESIGN: the whole archaeology chain is verified end to end, a bare press PDF through convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template to a live template, with one record per page confirmed for PDF output (page count equals row count, verified at three rows) and per row image binding confirmed visually through an at prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles. The frame granularity checkpoint rests on the documented finding that a continuous flow collapsed to exactly ONE TextFrame with ZERO graphic frames, and the offset hazard on the documented finding that textContent dropped a 17 character run while keeping its line break, the validator still returned VALID and prepare still reported success while only 3 of 5 mappings landed. Row order is taken through the PDF route, which is the route verified correct, never through multi record raster output, which came back REVERSED. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately, and no photograph is ever left as a URL. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. AVOIDED: no video_render, video_render_frame or video_metadata, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no variable QR, no bleed claim on a PDF derived template, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
